anti_overlap: Does NOT cover distribution channel strategy or version numbering policy (fd-typeface-release)
Does NOT cover scope boundary enforcement between v0.1 and deferred versions (fd-field-guide-publishing)
decision_lens: A kit that ships with one missing component fails completely — a partially-assembled pickup system produces noise, not music. Every dependency must ship or be explicitly declared external with a minimum-version check.
distance_rationale: Instrument kit makers ship bundles into an existing instrument (the practitioner's guitar) exactly as this distribution ships into an existing Hermes install — the 'additive overlay on a working host' pattern is identical, and the failure modes of partial assembly are directly isomorphic.
expected_isomorphisms: Binary presence check maps to 'does the solder bridge the right pads'; idempotent install maps to assembly instructions that produce the same result whether the pickup cavity was previously routed or not. Post-install smoke test maps to 'strum and check for 60Hz hum' — a quick signal-path verification before returning the instrument to the client.
focus: Reviews the distribution bundle through the lens of a musical instrument kit manufacturer — completeness of components, dependency sequencing, idempotent assembly instructions, and what happens when a practitioner installs into a partially-configured environment
name: fd-instrument-kit-packaging
persona: Apply the perspective of a boutique guitar electronics kit designer who ships active pickup systems requiring the luthier to already own a working guitar. They measure whether every component is present, whether assembly instructions assume the right prior state, whether the component list matches what ships, and whether a partial install leaves the instrument worse than before. They flag anything that requires the installer to improvise beyond the documented procedure.
review_areas: Component completeness: does the dist/v0.1/ bundle contain every file the install.sh references, with no implicit 'go get this elsewhere' for runtime-critical pieces?
Assembly sequencing: does install.sh perform steps in the correct dependency order — Hermes version check before copying skills, MCP registration after venv setup?
Partial-install safety: if install.sh fails midway (e.g., MCP build fails), does it leave the Hermes profile in a worse state than before, or does it clean up cleanly?

External dependency declaration: the auraken-lens binary is a declared external — does the installer verify it exists and emit a clear error if absent, rather than silently producing a broken MCP registration?

Platform-specific component variants: the brainstorm defers linux-amd64/arm64/darwin binaries — does v0.1 clearly surface which platforms are supported vs. untested rather than silently failing on unsupported ones?
Confirmation and next-steps handoff: after install, does the practitioner know the assembly worked — is there a smoke test step equivalent to 'pluck the string and check for signal'?

severity_examples.condition: Practitioner has a working Hermes setup before install and a broken one after, with no rollback path
severity_examples.scenario: install.sh references auraken-lens binary but does not verify its presence before writing MCP config — Hermes loads with a broken MCP registration that errors on every invocation

severity_examples.condition: No explicit post-install smoke test; practitioner discovers failure only when invoking /auraken in a real session
severity_examples.scenario: MCP venv creation fails silently and install.sh exits 0 — skills are copied but MCP server is not registered, producing a partial install the practitioner cannot diagnose

severity_examples.condition: Practitioner spends time debugging an unsupported platform rather than learning from a clear refusal
severity_examples.scenario: INSTALL.md describes a supported-platforms matrix that does not match what the installer actually validates — 'macOS: expected to work' claim with no installer guard leaves macOS users in an ambiguous state

source_domain: Boutique musical instrument kit manufacturing — active electronics for luthiers
success_hints: Install.sh should exit non-zero and print a clear diagnostic for every external dependency it cannot satisfy
A post-install smoke test (invoke auraken-lens once with a test prompt, verify exit 0) catches 80% of assembly failures before the practitioner ever opens a real session
Partial-install cleanup (trap EXIT with rollback) is the installer equivalent of 'undo soldering' — missing it means a failed install is worse than no install
task_context: Document for external review: a v0.1 publishable bundle (SKILL.md + MCP server + MANIFEST.yaml + install.sh) shipped as a GitHub release, intended for individual practitioners with a working Hermes Agent install. Review for bundle completeness, installer correctness, and practitioner-facing clarity.
